content: The reticuloendothelial system (RES) is a component of the immune system that is primarily composed of phagocytic cells, such as monocytes and macrophages, which are located in reticular connective tissue. These cells are concentrated in lymph nodes and the spleen. Additionally, Kupffer cells in the liver and tissue histiocytes are integral parts of the RES. The terms mononuclear phagocytic system and lymphoreticular system are often used interchangeably with RES. The system is categorized into primary and secondary lymphoid organs based on their roles. Primary Lymphoid Organs The primary, or central, lymphoid organs are the sites where the cells of the RES are generated. These cells are produced in the bone marrow. The thymus is also considered a primary lymphoid organ because it is essential for the maturation of T cells. Secondary Lymphoid Organs The secondary, or peripheral, lymphoid organs are the locations where the cells of the RES carry out their immune functions. These include the lymph nodes, spleen, and mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT). MALT is further subdivided into gut-associated lymphoid tissue (GALT) and bronchus-associated lymphoid tissue (BALT). Kupffer cells in the liver also contribute to the RES, but they are not organized into a specific tissue structure; instead, they are scattered throughout the liver sinusoids. Function The secondary lymphoid organs are responsible for monitoring all antigens that enter or circulate within the body and initiating an immune response when foreign antigens are detected. GALT and BALT are particularly exposed to antigens entering through the gastrointestinal and respiratory tracts, respectively. As extracellular fluid moves through the lymphatic system on its way back to systemic circulation, it passes through lymph nodes, where any antigens present in the interstitial fluid are processed. The spleen, on the other hand, filters the blood to identify antigens. When foreign antigens are detected, these tissues coordinate a robust and multifaceted immune response. Clinical Significance In individuals with haemochromatosis, the reticuloendothelial system becomes a site of iron accumulation. Additionally, lymphoma involving the reticuloendothelial system is referred to as reticuloendotheliosis.
